sentences.text: Titanichthys is an extinct genus of giant marine placoderms found in the shallow seas of the Late Devonian in Morocco, Eastern North America, and possibly Europe.
Scientists classify this animal as a basal aspinothoracid, a group most closely related to the genera Bungartius and Tafilalichthys.
This creature is considered the first known large-sized vertebrate filter feeder, possessing jaws functionally similar to those of baleen whales and basking sharks.
While once estimated to reach 7 to 7.6 meters in length, a 2023 study by Engelman suggests it was likely comparable to Dunkleosteus, measuring about 4.1 meters.

When geologist Henri Termier first found fossils of the species Titanichthys termieri, he initially placed them in the genus Gorgonichthys before convincing colleagues they belonged to a placoderm rather than a dinosaur.
Titanichthys lived during the Eifelian to Famennian stages, approximately 393.47 to 358.86 million years ago.
